post.caption: A rough yellow diamond of more than 287 carats was found in South Africa's Kimberley mine in 1877, and Charles Tiffany bought it for $18,000. Tiffany's gemologist George Kunz oversaw the cutting in Paris, which left a cushion cut stone of 128.54 carats with 82 facets. Mary Whitehouse wore it first in 1957, Audrey Hepburn wore it in 1961 photos for Breakfast at Tiffany's, and Lady Gaga wore it at the 2019 Oscars.
